nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 11.6°, 23.3°, 34.3°, 38.9°, 46.6°, 60.2°, and 61.5° indexed to NiFe LDH (PDF No. 38-0715); Ag peaks at 38.0° and 44.2° (111) and (002) faces (PDF No. 04-0783); (003) plane negatively shifted by 0.1° indicating Ru incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline phase composition of the products was assessed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns, as illustrated in Figure 1b. The peaks at 11.6°, 23.3°, 34.3°, 38.9°, 46.6°, 60.2°, and 61.5° are indexed to the diffraction peaks of NiFe LDH (PDF No. 38-0715) ... reflecting the inclusion of Ru into the NiFe LDH lattice.

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at ≈451 and 530 cm⁻¹ associated with A₁g stretching modes of Ni²⁺-OH and Ni²⁺-O; peak at ≈1580 cm⁻¹ attributed to Ag NPs; enhanced A₁g peaks due to surface plasmon resonance of Ag NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman peaks at ≈451 and 530 cm⁻¹ are associated with the A₁g stretching modes of the Ni²⁺-OH and Ni²⁺-O, respectively, and the peak located at ≈1580 cm⁻¹ is attributed to Ag NPs (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Vertical arrays of LDH nanosheets observed for all samples with no notable change in nanosheet morphology after Ru or Ag decoration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The catalyst morphology was further examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The vertical arrays of LDH nanosheets are observed for all the samples (Figure 1d and Figure S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice spacing of 0.252 nm corresponding to (012) plane of Ni(OH)₂; interplanar distances larger than pristine NiFe LDH (≈0.248 nm); Ag lattice spacing of 0.23 nm indexed to (111) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images of Ag/NiFeRu LDH exhibit the lattice spacing of 0.252 nm corresponding to the (012) plane of Ni(OH)₂ (Figure 1e,f) ... the lattice spacing of 0.23 nm is indexed to the (111) plane of metallic Ag on Ag/NiFeRu LDH (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Well-defined diffraction pattern indexed to (012) and (110) planes of Ni(OH)₂, and (111) plane of Ag.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern shows a well-defined diffraction pattern, indexed to the (012) and (110) planes of Ni(OH)₂, and (111) plane of Ag (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ru, Ni, Fe, and O elements; Ag elements show obvious segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping suggests the uniform distribution of Ru, Ni, Fe, and O elements (Figure 1h), while Ag elements have obvious segregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ag content 6.41 wt% and Ru content 0.20 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-mass spectroscopy shows that the contents of Ag and Ru species are 6.41 wt.% and 0.20 wt.% (Table S1, Supporting Information), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ag content 6.16% and Ru content 0.15 wt%, consistent with ICP-MS analysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: consistent with the energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) analysis of 6.16% for Ag and 0.15 wt.% for Ru, as illustrated in Figure S4, Supporting Information.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p spectra show Ni²⁺ at 854.6/872.2 eV and Ni³⁺ at 854.4/873.9 eV with Ni³⁺ content increasing to 50.86% in Ag/NiFeRu LDH; Fe 2p shows Fe³⁺ at 711.5/725.3 eV; Ru 3p reveals Ru⁰ and Ru³⁺ states; Ag 3d shifts from metallic Ag (367.6/373.6 eV) to Ag⁺ (367.0/373.1 eV) after Ru doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows that the Ni 2p spectra with the peak at binding energies of 854.6 eV and 872.2 eV correspond to the Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ spin-orbit peaks of Ni²⁺, while the peaks at 854.4 and 873.9 eV refer to Ni³⁺ ... the XPS spectrum of Ag/NiFeRu LDH shows the diffraction peaks located at 367.0 and 373.1 eV assigned as Ag⁺ 3d₃/₂ and Ag⁺ 3d₁/₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ag/NiFeRu LDH shows lowest R_ct of 1.393 Ω, indicating improved charge transfer ability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was implemented to investigate charge transfer dynamics (Figure 3e and Table S4, Supporting Information). Ag/NiFeRu LDH shows the lowest value (1.393 Ω) among all the catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl of Ag/NiFeRu LDH is 36.57 mF cm⁻², higher than NiFe LDH (5.10 mF cm⁻²), indicating high electrochemical active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical double-layer capacitances (C_dl) were evaluated according to the cyclic voltammetry curves (Figure S7, Supporting Information). From Figure 3f, the C_dl of the Ag/NiFeRu LDH (36.57 mF cm⁻²) is higher than those of NiFe LDH (5.10 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge absorption edges close to Fe₂O₃ for fresh catalysts; Ag/NiFeRu LDH shows higher valence Fe than NiFeRu LDH; smaller blue shift after OER for Ag/NiFeRu LDH indicating less Fe oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the absorption edges in the XANES spectra of fresh NiFeRu LDH and Ag/NiFeRu LDH on Fe K-edge are close to those of Fe₂O₃ ... Ag/NiFeRu LDH has a smaller blue shift compared to the NiFeRu LDH after OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-O coordination numbers increase after OER (NiFeRu LDH: 5.8→6.9, Ag/NiFeRu LDH: 5.9→6.6); Fe-Ni bond length shorter in Ag/NiFeRu LDH (2.50 Å vs 2.58 Å); less Fe segregation in Ag/NiFeRu LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS fitting results present that the Fe-O coordination numbers of both NiFeRu LDH (5.8 to 6.9) and Ag/NiFeRu LDH (5.9 to 6.6) increase after OER ... the Fe-Ni coordination number of Ag/NiFeRu LDH before and after OER ranges from 5.3 to 5.8.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni²⁺-OH/Ni²⁺-O peaks at 452/531 cm⁻¹ transform to Ni³⁺-OH/Ni³⁺-O at 472/547 cm⁻¹ from 1.4 V_RHE; Ag/NiFeRu LDH shows Ag₂O peaks at 692/1058 cm⁻¹ at 1.5 V_RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra were scanned in the potential window of 1.2-1.6 V_RHE ... two new peaks representing the Ag₂O peaks occur at 692 and 1058 cm⁻¹ as the potential was applied 1.5 V_RHE.
